transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I guess what brings me in is that I just can't seem to shake this heavy mix of fear and guilt. I'm basically tense all day, just... waiting for something else to go wrong. And I keep blaming myself for not stopping what happened.
Can you tell me about what happened that led to these feelings of fear and guilt? Was there a particular event or situation that started all of this?
Yeah. All of this started about four months ago. We were doing a porch repair at our house, and... well, my husband fell. It was a bad fall. And this has just been going on ever since that happened.

You mentioned this started about four months ago after your husband's fall. When did these feelings of fear, guilt, and tension actually begin—was it right after the fall happened, or did it take days or weeks before you started experiencing these feelings?

I'm not entirely sure, honestly. I mean, right after it happened, it was just... chaos, you know? Dealing with the hospital and everything. But I guess the fear and the guilt, being tense all the time... it feels like it's just been there since that day. I don't remember exactly when it settled in, but it hasn't really left since then.
Since your husband's fall, have you been having unwanted memories or flashbacks of what happened? Or do you find yourself reliving the event, even when you don't want to?

Yeah, I do. With my job as a building inspector, I'm around construction sites a lot, so... I'll just be doing something normal, like measuring a railing, or I'll hear a ladder scrape against a wall. And out of nowhere, I can see him falling. 

It's like it's happening right in front of me all over again. My stomach just drops, and my hands start getting shaky. So, yes, the memories definitely come back even when I really don't want them to.

Besides those moments when the memories come back unexpectedly, have you been deliberately avoiding things—like avoiding construction sites, or maybe avoiding going near porches or ladders—because they remind you of your husband's fall?

Yeah, I have. I mean, at work, I've actually started turning down jobs if they involve raised porches or second-story decks. I just pass them on to someone else if I can. And at home... I find excuses not to talk about the repair at all. I don't even like looking at the spot where it happened, so I just try to avoid that area completely.

Have you noticed that you're more easily startled than you used to be—like if someone taps you on the shoulder or a door slams, you jump more than normal? Or do you find yourself constantly on edge, scanning your surroundings?

I haven't really noticed being more jumpy, no. I mean, loud noises don't bother me any more than they used to. And I don't feel like I'm constantly on edge or looking out for danger everywhere I go. It's just... mostly when I'm reminded of the fall, like I mentioned before. But otherwise, no, I don't think I'm easily startled.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to concentrate or focus on things? For example, at work or when reading, do you find it harder to keep your attention on what you're doing?

No, I haven't really noticed any issues with that. When I'm working on a site—as long as it's not a porch or a deck like I mentioned—I can focus on my inspections just fine. And reading or doing paperwork at home hasn't been a problem either. My concentration seems pretty normal.

Since the fall happened, have you noticed that you feel emotionally numb or disconnected from things—like you're having trouble feeling joy or interest in activities you used to enjoy, or feeling distant from people close to you?

No, I wouldn't say I feel numb or anything like that. I still care about my family just the same, and I haven't lost interest in my hobbies or anything. I don't feel distant from anyone. It's really just the stuff related to the accident that bothers me.

When you think back to right after your husband's fall, did you start experiencing these feelings of fear, guilt, and tension within the first few days or weeks, or did they develop more gradually over time?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. Um, right after he fell, everything was just... a lot to deal with. We were so focused on the hospital and his recovery, so I don't really know if the guilt and the fear started in those first few days or if it kind of crept up on me later on. I just know it's been bothering me for a while now, but I couldn't really give you an exact timeline.

Looking back, do you remember if you were already experiencing this intense fear and guilt while your husband was still in the hospital being treated, or did those feelings start after he came home and you had more time to process what happened?

I really couldn't say for sure. Like I said, everything was just such a blur back then. While he was in the hospital, I was just focused on him getting better and making sure he was okay. I wasn't really paying attention to how I was feeling. So, I don't know if it started then or after he came home. I just know it's been a problem for a while.
In those first few days right after your husband fell—like within the first 3 days or so—do you remember if you were already having that intense fear and guilt, or did those feelings come later?

I honestly don't know. Like I was saying, I just wasn't focused on myself at all during that time. Those first few days were all about his injuries and what the doctors were saying. I can't really pinpoint if the fear and the guilt were there right at the beginning or if they showed up a week or two later. I just don't have a clear memory of when my own feelings started.

When your husband first fell and went to the hospital, do you remember what you were feeling in those very first 24 hours—were you already experiencing that intense fear and guilt then, or do you think those feelings came later?

I really just don't know how else to explain it. I can't remember what I was feeling in those first 24 hours. I was just... I was just trying to get through it. I couldn't tell you if the guilt was there on day one or day ten. I just don't know.

Looking back now, do you think these feelings of fear and guilt started happening pretty much right around the time of the fall itself, or do you think they came on later—maybe after a week or more had passed?

Doc, I really don't have a different answer for you. Like I've been saying, I honestly can't tell you if it was right when it happened or a week later. I'm sorry, I just don't have a timeline for when the guilt started. My brain just wasn't logging how I felt back then, so I really can't give you an exact day.
